column3: The Hebrew pairs an active closing form with a passive closed form; BSB combines them as “tightly shut up.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew makes the seven priests the direct subject of carrying; BSB casts this as the command “Have seven priests carry.”

The Hebrew explicitly names “the sound of the horn,” says the wall falls “under itself,” and describes each man going up opposite him; BSB uses “its sound,” “collapse,” and charging straight into the city.
The Hebrew directly states that seven priests will carry the horns; BSB says to “have seven priests carry” them.

Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew ends with verbs for going and blowing the horns; BSB recasts this as the horns continuing to sound.
The Hebrew actively prohibits causing the voice to be heard; BSB uses “let your voice be heard.”
The Hebrew repeats “the camp”; BSB uses “there” for the second occurrence. BSB also supplies “carried” in describing the ark’s circuit.
The Hebrew says “in the morning” without an explicit word “next”; BSB supplies “next.”

The Hebrew calls the men “messengers”; BSB calls them “spies.”
The Hebrew addresses the people in the plural; BSB uses singular “you yourself” in the warning about being set apart.
The Hebrew repeats the LORD’s name and uses a singular collective pronoun for the holy objects; BSB uses “His treasury” and plural “they.”

The Hebrew initially says the people shouted “and they blew the horns”; BSB makes the sounding a “when” clause. The Hebrew says the wall fell “under itself” and each man went up opposite him; BSB has “collapsed” and charging straight into the city.
The Hebrew says “by the mouth of the sword” and uses singular collective names for the ox, sheep, and donkey; BSB has “at the edge of the sword” and plural animal names.
The Hebrew says “all that belongs to her” and uses the verb for swearing; BSB has “all who are with her” and “promised.”
The Hebrew has plural “all her families”; BSB says singular “her whole family.”
The Hebrew uses an unnamed plural subject and explicitly says “with fire”; BSB names “the Israelites” and says “burned up.”
The Hebrew calls the men “messengers”; BSB calls them “the men.”
The Hebrew says to “build” the city and names its “doors”; BSB says “rebuilds” and “gates.”
The Hebrew says his report or fame “was” in all the land; BSB supplies the action “spread.”
